name: Malachi Lee
strengths: Lee stacks corners on vertical go-routes and creates clear separation once he gets over the top.
Lee tracks deep balls over his shoulder cleanly and high-points contested catches in traffic.
Lee is linear and urgent after the catch — runs through arm tackles and turns short throws into chunk YAC.
Lee also plays safety (#1 WR/SS) — ballhawk traits show up with production (7 INTs on the sophomore reel).
weaknesses: Lee still needs mass on the 6-2 / 185 frame to finish through SEC press — most of this reel is off-coverage looks.
Lee wins more linear than lateral — COD/wiggle after the catch is not the primary separator yet.
comparison: Lee comps to Romeo Doubs — 6-2 perimeter WR mold who wins vertically with length, tracking, and outside separation (size-matched within ~1–2" of Lee's 6-2 / 185).
projection: Lee projects as Year 1 package/rotation WR snaps, then compete for a starting perimeter job by Year 2 — ceiling is every-down SEC WR who takes the top off coverage and finishes contested.
schemeFit: Lee fits a Faulkner-style rhythm room that wants a lengthy outside WR who can stretch the field and win over the top.
insiderNotes: Lee is a 4-star 2028 WR from Loudoun Sports Academy (formerly Westfield), listed 6-2 / 185. Hudl 'End of Sophomore Season Highlights' (~5:48): vertical stack/go separation, over-the-shoulder tracking, contested high-points, linear YAC, two-way SS production. Florida offered Aug 27, 2026 (Lee announced). Comp: Romeo Doubs.
